newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS UNVEIL NEW CAR ON CAUTIOUS NOTE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-WILLIAMS UNVEIL NEW CAR ON CAUTIOUS NOTE.

text.p: Defending champions Williams unveiled their new FW19 car which will carry their challenge in this year's Formula One World Championship on Friday amid cautious tones from team chief Frank Williams and his drivers.

Williams, who said he was delighted to have signed a new two-year deal with Meccachrome of France to supply them with Renault engines in 1998 and 1999, would not be drawn into making any rash predictions on the season ahead.

After the car had been unveiled at the team's former headquarters, Williams said he was looking forward to the new season and did not expect the impending Imola trial, at which he will be facing charges of manslaughter following the death of Ayrton Senna in 1994, to effect his commitment.

In answer to a question about maintaining his and the team's motivation, Williams said: "It will be business as usual. I do not believe it will have any effect at all on myself, Patrick Head or anyone involved in the running of our team throughout the season."
Williams and Head are due to face charges at Imola on February 20.
Head said the new car was from the same family as its predecessors.
"Although we have followed the same theme, the FW19 is a completely new car," he said.
"It has a new transverse transmission, allows for the innovative Renault RS9 engine and satisfies the 1997 steering and rear impact test."
The car was designed by Williams chief designer Adrian Newey who was absent on Friday because he is locked in a contractural dispute with the team.

Williams' drivers Jacques Villeneuve of Canada and Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany were both reluctant to sound over-optimistic despite being installed as favourites to succeed Briton Damon Hill as drivers' champion and retaining the team's constructors' crown.
Villeneuve said: "It would be great to feel like a favourite but it would be dangerous as well."
Frentzen said: "People expect a lot from me and they are right. I expect a lot of myself and the team is well prepared and so am I."
